about: docs/24 as DATA (ADR-0019 decision 6: adding a source is a data change). One row per channel: where it lives, what to read, the evidence roles it can yield, and the EXACT local Agent Reach commands the connected agent runs on the user's own machine for one search intent. Generic template code (python/executors.py) fills {query} and the receipt tags; no code branches on a channel name. Commands follow Agent Reach v1.5.0 (references: social, video, search, web) and the supplier hand-off measured 2026-11-01 (Exa requires `objective`; a query value never starts with @).

never: do not use your agent's built-in web search, web fetch or browser for this research
do not run these commands on the Polymath host: they run on the user's own machine, in the user's own Agent Reach setup
never solve, skip or work around a sign-in or a human check: record the source in limitations as needing the user

placeholders: A token in angle brackets (<post_id>, <video_url>, <url>, <PRODUCT_URL>, ...) is filled from the previous command's output, as `fill` says; everything else is exact.

PRODUCT_REALITY_CHECK: relation: competitor | substitute | current_solution | validates | solves
SUPPLIER_RESEARCH: supplier: <supplier name as shown, or none>

reddit.why: first-person complaint, workaround, and comparison language

fill.<post_id>: the id of each relevant post in the search output

receipt_tags: community: <the subreddit the thread is in>
moment: <before | during | transition | after, when the post says>
workaround: <what they do instead, when the post says>
reddit.requires: Reddit has no zero-config path: the user's logged-in Chrome (OpenCLI) or an rdt-cli login; check `agent-reach doctor --json` first

amazon_reviews.why: post-purchase language: what broke, what they did instead, what they compared it to
amazon_reviews.law: a review is a product complaint or request, never FRICTION_EVIDENCE about life without the product (docs/04)
alternatives: objective=Amazon product pages for {query} with their customer reviews and questions

fill.<asin_or_url>: an ASIN or product URL from the search output
fill.<url>: a product page URL from the search output

amazon_reviews.requires: OpenCLI's amazon adapter (Chrome open with the OpenCLI extension); `opencli list` shows it

youtube.collect: the comment threads under the top demonstration videos (cite the video's youtube.com/watch URL; date = the comment's date)

fill.<video_url>: a video's https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id> URL from the search output; the comments are in the .info.json `comments` field

receipt_tags: moment: <before | during | transition | after, when the comment says>
youtube.requires: yt-dlp (Agent Reach installs it); comments are best effort

tiktok.why: short-video comment threads, captions and on-screen text where people show and discuss the workaround
tiktok.limits: OpenCLI reads videos, not their comment threads — quote the caption/on-screen text, or read comments through the browser lane
tiktok.collect: the comment threads under the top videos (cite each video as tiktok.com/@creator/video/<id>, never a short link; date = the comment's date)
alternatives: objective=TikTok videos (tiktok.com/@creator/video/<id>) where people show or discuss {query}

fill.<video_url>: a video's canonical https://www.tiktok.com/@creator/video/<id> URL from the search output

tiktok.requires: OpenCLI's tiktok adapter (Chrome open with the OpenCLI extension), else the Exa search

instagram.why: comment threads under public Reels and posts where people show and discuss the workaround
instagram.limits: Agent Reach's Instagram channel (OpenCLI) searches users and reads an account's recent posts, not comment threads: find Reels by the Exa search, quote the caption; public posts only, read occasionally (never in bulk), never quote a username
instagram.collect: the comment threads under public Reels and posts (cite instagram.com/reel/<id> or instagram.com/p/<id>; date = the comment's date)
commands: objective=Public Instagram Reels (instagram.com/reel/<id>) where people show or discuss {query}

fill.<username>: the account of a relevant Reel from the search output (never quote the username in the receipt)

instagram.requires: the user's logged-in Chrome with the OpenCLI extension for `opencli instagram`; the Exa search needs nothing

xiaohongshu.why: consumer notes + threaded comments (Chinese; translate the quote, keep the original)
xiaohongshu.collect: consumer notes and their comment threads

fill.<note_id>: a note id from the search output (use the full result URL or id: a bare note id without its xsec_token does not read)

xiaohongshu.requires: the user's own Chrome session (OpenCLI) or xiaohongshu-mcp with cookies the user exported; never log in for the user

twitter.why: public complaint and comparison language in threads
twitter.collect: public posts and their reply threads

fill.<tweet_url_or_id>: a post's URL or id from the search output (the reply thread comes with it)

twitter.requires: twitter-cli with TWITTER_AUTH_TOKEN and TWITTER_CT0 set in the same shell (never echo them), or OpenCLI

forum.why: niche practitioners describing real behavior and adaptations
forum.collect: threads where practitioners describe real behavior and adaptations
commands: objective=Forum threads where practitioners describe {query}: real behaviour, workarounds and frictions, with their dates

fill.<url>: a thread URL from the search output

receipt_tags: community: <the forum and board the thread is in>
forum.requires: Agent Reach's Exa channel (mcporter) and curl

amazon_listings.why: who already sells THIS concept: the listing, its price and its reviews
amazon_listings.collect: product listings: title, price as listed, rating and review count
alternatives: objective=Amazon product listings for {query}: product name, price, rating and review count

fill.<asin_or_url>: an ASIN or product URL from the search output
fill.<url>: a product page URL from the search output

amazon_listings.requires: OpenCLI's amazon adapter (Chrome open with the OpenCLI extension), else the Exa search

retail_web.why: existing products and substitutes on retailer and brand pages
retail_web.collect: product pages: name, price as listed, what it claims to solve
commands: objective=Product pages from retailers and brands selling {query}: product name, price and what it claims to solve

fill.<url>: a product page URL from the search output

retail_web.requires: Agent Reach's Exa channel (mcporter) and curl

youtube_reviews.why: hands-on reviews and comparison videos of the products already on the market
youtube_reviews.collect: review videos and the comment threads under them (cite the youtube.com/watch URL)

fill.<video_url>: a review video's https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id> URL from the search output

alibaba.why: manufacturer listings: tier prices, minimum order and supplier
alibaba.rule: Alibaba: tier price + MOQ text as shown
commands: objective=Individual alibaba.com product-detail pages (alibaba.com/product-detail/..._<number>.html) for: {query}. Rank single product pages first; exclude showroom, category, supplier-home and search pages. Pull the title, the price or the price tiers with their quantities, the minimum order (MOQ), the supplier company name and its years on Alibaba, units sold and reviews.

fill.<PRODUCT_URL>: a product page URL from step 1 (https://www.alibaba.com/product-detail/<name>_<number>.html)

parse.then: send each command's whole output, unedited, as its own supplier_parse call

alibaba.requires: Agent Reach's Exa channel (mcporter) and curl; Alibaba is read only this way (no host API)

cjdropshipping.why: dropship listings: per-unit price, minimum order (usually 1) and warehouse
cjdropshipping.rule: CJ: per-unit price incl. processing, MOQ is usually 1 — record ship-from warehouse
commands: objective=Individual CJdropshipping product pages (cjdropshipping.com/product/...-p-<id>.html) for: {query}. Rank single product pages first; exclude search, category, login and verification pages. Pull the title, the price in US dollars, the SKU and the shipping details.

fill.<PRODUCT_URL>: a product page URL from step 1 (https://cjdropshipping.com/product/<name>-p-<id>.html)

parse.then: send each command's whole output, unedited, as its own supplier_parse call

cjdropshipping.requires: the CJ API answers first on the Polymath host (the step's draft receipt); these commands are the fallback when it fails

1688.why: domestic Chinese wholesale listings (translate the title, keep the original)
1688.rule: 1688: tier price in CNY + MOQ text as shown
commands: objective=Individual 1688.com offer pages for: {query}. Pull the title, the price tiers with their quantities, the minimum order and the supplier.

fill.<PRODUCT_URL>: an offer page URL from step 1

1688.requires: Agent Reach's Exa channel (mcporter) and curl
